result.title: BATMoS: Budget-Aware Guidance Allocation for Efficient Video Diffusion
result.summary: The effectiveness of a video diffusion model's inference budget depends on where computation is spent along the denoising trajectory. Across eight equal-budget inference configurations, VBench total scores span 4.80 points, highlighting the importance of explicit allocation design. Our key insight is that guidance evaluations are not equally valuable across diffusion time: retaining the sampling updates while selectively reusing guidance can preserve generation quality with fewer denoiser evaluations. We introduce BATMoS (Budget Aware Temporal Mixture of Strategies), which routes between fresh classifier-free guidance and cached guidance using a single pretrained denoiser. A magnitude-based temporal rule assigns guidance reuse to low-magnitude blocks and reserves fresh guidance for the remaining blocks, with a single integer controlling the computation budget. The resulting schedule requires no additional router training or per-budget threshold search. Evaluated on CogVideoX-2B with 4,720 videos per configuration across all sixteen official VBench dimensions, BATMoS achieves the highest total score among the eight allocation policies and comes within 0.10 points of full classifier-free guidance using 20\% fewer branch evaluations. BATMoS also composes with feature reuse, reducing computation from 80 to 62 effective branch evaluations with a 0.11-point decrease in total score. These findings make temporal guidance allocation a practical mechanism for extracting more generation quality from a fixed inference budget.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究视频扩散模型固定推理预算在去噪时间轴上的分配问题，提出 BATMoS：依据幅值的时间规则在新鲜 classifier-free guidance 与缓存 guidance 之间路由，用单一整数控制预算，并在 CogVideoX-2B 的 VBench 十六维上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「沿轨迹不同阶段的算力价值不相等、可缓存复用少量评估」的预算分配框架，可能为 LVR 中动态计算预算与 latent 状态复用的策略设计和评价提供类比线索，但对象是视频生成 guidance，迁移性需人工核查。
